# Susan Baker

## Overview

- **Age:** elderly  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052)</sub>
- **Role:** Maid-of-all-work and housekeeper for the Blythe family  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Susan is a grim-faced, gray-looking spinster who admits she is no beauty. She keeps her hands busy with house work or knitting and is often accompanied by the aroma of her cooking. Her presence is described as that of a beneficent guardian spirit.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005), [v4 c24 P0](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0000), [v4 c35 P16](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0016), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000), [v5 c2 P5](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0005)_

## Personality

Susan is a fiercely loyal, kind-hearted, and pragmatic woman who takes immense pride in her household duties and cooking. She is highly opinionated, outspoken, and quick to express her views on local gossip, religion, and church politics. Despite her stern exterior and strict ideas about discipline, she possesses deep warmth, a penchant for romantic musings, and a tender devotion to children—especially young Shirley Blythe.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c19 P5](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0005), [v4 c22 P8](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0008), [v4 c24 P0](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0000), [v4 c24 P9](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0009), [v4 c35 P17](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0017), [v5 c1 P4](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0004), [v5 c1 P5](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0005), [v5 c1 P9](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0009), [v5 c2 P46](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0046), [v5 c26 P9](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0009)_

## History

Susan Baker was hired as maid-of-all-work at the little house in Four Winds when Anne and Gilbert Blythe were expecting their first child. She quickly devoted herself completely to Anne, fiercely taking charge of the household and mourning deeply when Anne's firstborn died. Susan remained as the permanent housekeeper and moved with the family when they relocated to Ingleside in Glen St. Mary. Following the birth of Anne's son Shirley, during which Anne was gravely ill, Susan cared for the infant with intense maternal tenderness and considered him her special baby. She faithfully managed the Ingleside house, cooked, knitted, defended the family against local gossip, and raised all the Blythe children.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c19 P0](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0000), [v4 c19 P18](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0018), [v4 c22 P0](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0000), [v4 c40 P41](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0041), [v4 c40 P43](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0043), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000), [v5 c1 P4](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0004), [v5 c1 P5](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0005), [v5 c1 P7](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0007)_

## Quotes

> Now for breakfast. I am of the opinion that we will all be glad of a bite and sup. You tell young Mrs. Doctor not to worry about a single thing—Susan is at the helm. You tell her just to think of her baby.  <sub>[v4 c19 P10](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0010)</sub>

> I am an old maid, but you never hear ME abusing the men. I like 'em. I would have married one if I could.  <sub>[v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005)</sub>

> Cats is cats, and take my word for it, they will never be anything else.  <sub>[v4 c40 P6](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0006)</sub>

> I gave him life just as much as you did, Mrs. Dr. dear. He is just as much my baby as he is yours.  <sub>[v5 c1 P5](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0005)</sub>

> I have never thought I was, and so I go calmly along. Not but what it has sometimes occurred to me that things might be run a little better than they are.  <sub>[v5 c26 P9](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0009)</sub>
